questions.context: Two seedlings have the same soil and water. One grows in bright light; the other stays in shade.
questions.prompt: What should the class measure to compare their growth?
questions.answer: the seedlings' heights each day
questions.explanation: Measuring growth over time gives evidence for comparing the plants.

questions.context: A magnet picks up a steel paper clip but not a wooden pencil.
questions.prompt: Which claim is best supported by the observation?
choices: the paper clip was attracted to the magnet
all materials are attracted to magnets
questions.answer: the paper clip was attracted to the magnet
questions.explanation: The test only shows how the two objects responded.

questions.context: A small puddle is marked with chalk. It becomes smaller during a warm sunny afternoon without anyone wiping it.
questions.prompt: What most likely happened to some of the water?
questions.answer: it evaporated into the air
questions.explanation: Liquid water can change into water vapor.

questions.context: A flashlight points at a toy dinosaur. Its shadow falls on the wall behind the toy.
questions.prompt: What caused the shadow?
choices: the toy blocked some of the light
the wall made its own darkness
questions.answer: the toy blocked some of the light
questions.explanation: Shadows form when an object blocks light.

questions.context: Students predict which surface a toy car will roll farthest on: carpet, tile or grass.
questions.prompt: What should they do after making a prediction?
choices: test each surface using the same starting position
choose the result they like best
change the toy car for every surface
questions.answer: test each surface using the same starting position
questions.explanation: A fair test holds other important conditions constant.

questions.context: Small fish eat water insects, and a heron eats the fish.
questions.prompt: Which animal could be affected if there were fewer water insects?
questions.answer: the small fish
questions.explanation: With less insect food, the small fish may have difficulty finding enough to eat.

questions.context: A beaver builds its home beside a freshwater stream.
questions.prompt: Which feature of the habitat helps the beaver most?
choices: snow on every day of the year
questions.answer: water and nearby woody plants
questions.explanation: The stream and plants help meet the beaver's needs.

questions.context: A windsock points toward the east because the wind blows it in that direction.
questions.prompt: What is a windsock useful for observing?
choices: the direction the air is moving
the exact weight of every cloud
questions.answer: the direction the air is moving
questions.explanation: The windsock moves with flowing air.

questions.context: Students find a shell-shaped fossil in a rock that formed long ago.
questions.prompt: What does the fossil provide?
choices: evidence that a living thing existed in the past
the exact age of every nearby rock
questions.answer: evidence that a living thing existed in the past
questions.explanation: Fossils preserve clues about past living things.

questions.context: Maya drops two similar balls from the same height.
questions.prompt: What pulls the balls toward the ground?
questions.answer: gravity
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls objects toward Earth.

questions.context: A student tests cloth, paper and plastic to build a rain cover.
questions.prompt: Which material property matters most?
choices: how well the material keeps water out
whether the material smells like flowers
how many letters are in its name
questions.answer: how well the material keeps water out
questions.explanation: A rain cover needs to resist water.

questions.context: The moon looks bright in the night sky.
questions.prompt: Where does most of the light we see from the moon come from?
choices: a fire burning on the moon
light emitted by the moon itself
questions.answer: sunlight reflected from its surface
questions.explanation: The moon reflects sunlight.

questions.context: A seedling uses water, grows and makes new leaves.
questions.prompt: Which observation shows it is a living thing?
choices: it grows and responds to its environment
questions.answer: it grows and responds to its environment
questions.explanation: Growth is one of several characteristics of living things.

questions.context: A piece of chocolate softens and melts in a warm room.
questions.prompt: What changed?
choices: the number of atoms in it
questions.answer: its physical state
questions.explanation: Melting changes a solid into a liquid without creating a new substance.

questions.context: A sunflower makes seeds after it grows and flowers.
questions.prompt: What can happen to a seed when conditions are suitable?
choices: it can germinate and become a new plant
it turns into a plastic bottle
questions.answer: it can germinate and become a new plant
questions.explanation: Germination begins the growth of a new plant.

questions.context: A stretched rubber band makes a sound when plucked.
questions.prompt: What is the band doing while it makes the sound?
questions.answer: vibrating
questions.explanation: Sound is produced by vibrations.

questions.context: One bean plant gets lots of water and another gets much less. They are different varieties and grow in different soil.
questions.prompt: Why is it hard to tell whether water caused any difference?
choices: more than one important condition changed
questions.answer: more than one important condition changed
questions.explanation: A fair comparison should change one main factor at a time.

questions.context: A class records outdoor temperature at the same time each day for 10 days.
questions.prompt: What can the records help show?
choices: how temperatures changed across the days
questions.answer: how temperatures changed across the days
questions.explanation: Repeated observations can reveal patterns over time.

questions.context: After heavy rain, a hillside has new grooves where soil washed downhill.
questions.prompt: Which process is shown?
questions.answer: erosion
questions.explanation: Moving water can carry away soil and rock particles.

questions.context: Two identical cups hold warm water. One has a thick sleeve and stays warmer longer.
questions.prompt: Which conclusion fits the observation?
choices: the sleeve created extra hot water
questions.answer: the sleeve slowed heat transfer
questions.explanation: Insulation slows the transfer of thermal energy.

questions.context: A toy car travels farther on a smooth ramp than on the same ramp covered with rough felt.
questions.prompt: What is a likely reason?
choices: the car no longer has wheels
questions.answer: rough felt creates more friction
questions.explanation: Friction resists motion and can change how far an object travels.

questions.context: A paper clip moves toward a magnet even before the magnet touches it.
questions.prompt: What does this show?
choices: magnetic force can act at a distance
magnets need to touch every object
metal paper clips always move away
questions.answer: magnetic force can act at a distance
questions.explanation: Magnetic forces can act without direct contact.

questions.context: A student shines a flashlight onto a mirror, and the light changes direction.
questions.prompt: Which process explains the change?
questions.answer: reflection
questions.explanation: Light can bounce off reflective surfaces.

questions.context: Bees visit flowering plants. Fewer bees visit the garden this season.
questions.prompt: What effect might occur?
choices: some plants may produce fewer seeds
questions.answer: some plants may produce fewer seeds
questions.explanation: Some flowering plants rely on animal pollinators.

questions.context: Two groups grow radishes under equal light and water. One uses sandy soil, the other uses clay-rich soil.
questions.prompt: Which factor are they testing?
questions.answer: soil type
questions.explanation: Soil type is the intentionally changed variable.

questions.context: A lamp connected to a battery turns off when a switch opens.
questions.prompt: Why does the lamp go out?
choices: the path for electric current is broken
the battery loses all its mass
questions.answer: the path for electric current is broken
questions.explanation: A closed circuit is needed for current to flow.

questions.context: Moist air cools, and tiny droplets form on the outside of a cold glass.
questions.prompt: Which process made the droplets?
questions.answer: condensation
questions.explanation: Water vapor cools and changes to liquid drops.

questions.context: A student measures a flagpole's shadow at noon and again late in the afternoon.
questions.prompt: What can cause the shadow to change length?
choices: the Sun's apparent position in the sky
a change in the flagpole's name
questions.answer: the Sun's apparent position in the sky
questions.explanation: The angle of incoming sunlight changes during the day.

questions.context: Two kinds of fossil footprints appear in an ancient rock layer.
questions.prompt: What can scientists most reasonably learn?
choices: some animals moved through that area in the past
the exact colors of every animal
questions.answer: some animals moved through that area in the past
questions.explanation: Tracks preserve evidence of ancient movement.

questions.context: Grass is eaten by rabbits, and foxes eat rabbits. The rabbit population becomes much smaller.
questions.prompt: Which change could follow?
questions.answer: foxes may find less food
questions.explanation: Food-web changes can affect consumers higher in the chain.

questions.context: A student compares how quickly sugar dissolves in cold and warm water. She uses equal sugar amounts and equal water volumes.
questions.prompt: What is the changed variable?
questions.answer: water temperature
questions.explanation: Only water temperature is deliberately varied.

questions.context: A class launches paper planes. A new design goes farther once, but not in later trials.
questions.prompt: What should the class do before claiming it is better?
choices: repeat fair tests and compare the results
ignore the flights that went a shorter distance
questions.answer: repeat fair tests and compare the results
questions.explanation: Repeated tests reduce the influence of unusual results.

questions.context: Solar panels generate electricity on a bright day but less on a cloudy one.
questions.prompt: Which factor affects their output?
choices: the amount of sunlight reaching them
questions.answer: the amount of sunlight reaching them
questions.explanation: Solar panels use energy from sunlight.

questions.context: A river rises after a storm. A map shows lower land near the banks.
questions.prompt: Which area is more likely to flood first?
choices: the upper floor of a tall building
questions.answer: low ground near the river
questions.explanation: Water can spread over nearby low-lying land when rivers rise.

questions.context: A new road divides a forest into two smaller habitats.
questions.prompt: Why might this be a problem for some animals?
choices: it can make it harder to reach food or mates
every animal prefers living near cars
roads increase the number of trees
questions.answer: it can make it harder to reach food or mates
questions.explanation: Habitat fragmentation can limit animal movement.

questions.context: A bridge model fails under a load. The team studies where it bent and changes the supports.
questions.prompt: What should the team do next?
choices: claim it is perfect without testing
questions.answer: test the improved model again
questions.explanation: Engineering designs are revised and tested based on evidence.
